To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a combination of a high model of end stage disease score and a low indocyanine green plasma disappearance rate is associated with a longer stay in the intensive unit care, a longer stay in hospital and higher mortality in liver transplantation recipients.

a combination of a high model of end stage-liver-disease score (MELDs) and low indocyanine green plasma disappearance rate (ICG-PD) predicts a significant prolonged stay in the ICU as well as in the hospital and a hospital mortality rate of 40% in liver transplant patients.
a combination of the MELD score with the ICG-PDR predicts a significant longer ICU stay, a significant longer hospital stay and a higher hospital mortality in liver transplantation recipients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an early postoperative tool for the prediction of outcome in liver transplant patients.
the development of a new, easy-to-use and non-invasive method to predict outcome in liver transplant patients.
a new, non-invasive, early postoperative method of predicting length of stay in ICU and length of stay in hospital in liver transplant recipients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combination of MELDS score and ICG-PDR is a valuable predictor for length of stay and hospital mortality in patients after liver transplantation and should be considered as an important part of the intensive care management.
this combination is a valuable tool for the management of liver transplant patients.
the combination of MELDscores and a singular IGC-PDR measurement in liver transplant recipients in the early post operative phase is an accurate prediction tool for outcome in liver recipients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MELD score is the best single predictor for length of stay and hospital mortality, while the combination of MELDs and ICG-PDR is the best predictor for length of ICU stay.
the combination of a high preoperative MELD score with a singular early postoperative ICG-PDR test is an accurate predictor of outcome in liver transplant candidates.
a low ICG clearance is associated with a poor prognosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of MELDScore and ICG-PDR is a good predictor of ICU length of stay, hospital length of stay and hospital mortality.
the combination of MELDs and ICG-PDRs is a powerful tool to predict the outcome of liver transplantation.

the combination of a high pre-operative MELD score (>25) with an early post-operative indocyanine green test (ICG-PD) clearance of less than 20%/minute is a strong predictor of poor outcome (longer stay in the intensive-care unit and hospital, and high hospital mortality) in liver transplant recipients.
